title: Band-9 Samples: Where would you like to travel in the future? [Why?]
passage_text: This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 10 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 4 Test 3 question: “Where would you like to travel in the future? [Why?]” Sample 1 Female Male As a person who hasn’t traveled much, I’m keen to explore the different regions of my own country first. I see it as a stepping stone to global exploration. Familiarizing myself with the diverse cultures, landscapes, and experiences within my homeland would build my confidence and equip me with the necessary skills for more ambitious travels abroad in the future. Sample 2 Female Male In the future, I plan to travel across my own country primarily because it’s a cost-effective way to indulge my wanderlust. The savings on international flight costs alone allow for a more extended and in-depth exploration of my nation’s heritage, natural beauty, and diverse traditions. It’s a win-win situation – I get the joy of travel, and my wallet stays relatively unscathed! Sample 3 Female Male I’m particularly excited about the prospect of traveling to America, mainly because it offers an authentic environment to practice English. Conversing with locals, navigating through cities, and even simple activities like ordering food would provide practical language experiences that could significantly enhance my English fluency. Sample 4 Female Male I’ve always had a penchant for gastronomy, and Vietnam is one country I’d love to tour next. Vietnamese cuisine is renowned for its balance of flavors and fresh ingredients. I’m eager to stroll through the bustling markets of Hanoi, sample local delicacies from street vendors, and perhaps even learn to cook some traditional dishes. Sample 5 Female Male I am particularly eager to set foot in Japan. I’m fascinated by its rich cultural heritage and the seamless blend of tradition and modernity. From visiting ancient temples in Kyoto to witnessing the hustle and bustle of Tokyo, it feels like every corner has a story to tell. Plus, I am a huge fan of sushi, and I can’t wait to try it in its birthplace. Sample 6 Female Male I’ve been contemplating volunteer tourism for quite some time, and Africa stands out as my preferred destination. I’m drawn to the idea of making a tangible difference in underprivileged communities while soaking up the local culture. Plus, the continent’s diverse wildlife and breathtaking landscapes are an added bonus. Sample 7 Female Male I’ve always been enthralled by the richness of ancient history, and for that reason, I’d love to traverse the vast landscapes of China someday. It’s a treasure trove of ancient wonders like the Great Wall and the Terracotta Army, which I’ve only seen in pictures. I’m eager to experience these marvels up close and delve into the compelling stories they hold. Sample 8 Female Male Dubai has always been on my bucket list. The city’s rapid transformation from a barren desert into a metropolis of sky-high buildings and cutting-edge technology fascinates me. The blend of traditional Arabian culture with modern architectural marvels makes it a unique destination. Sample 9 Female Male I find myself in a bit of a quandary when it comes to pinning down one particular destination for future travel. The world is a vast, vibrant canvas of cultures, landscapes, and experiences, and I am open to the idea of exploring any part of it. The thrill, for me, is not just in the destination, but also in the journey and the unexpected discoveries along the way. Sample 10 Female Male To be perfectly honest, I haven’t really given much thought to where I might venture to in the future. My current professional commitments are so demanding that virtually all of my energy is dedicated to meeting those challenges. Once I’ve navigated through this busy phase, I’ll certainly take some time to ponder about potential destinations.
